title: Quoro event
description: One Quoro event. The envelope is identical everywhere it appears: on the SSE stream (GET /api/v1/events/stream), in GET /api/v1/events, in webhook delivery bodies, and in node-agent `event` messages. A node-agent `event` message carries the same envelope without `seq`: the node assigns `id` when it emits the event, and the primary assigns `seq` on receipt, so `seq` is required for every event that a client reads from the API, the stream or a webhook. The node-agent protocol document defines that message form. The `$id` URL is a placeholder identifier; this schema is published inside the repository, not fetched from that address. Payloads are additive within schema_version 1. Id prefixes, status enums and event types are the shared vocabulary of docs/contracts/README.md; the event log is the notify step of the AI-native loop (D-0032) and the envelope carries the incident and grant context that the loop needs (D-0030, D-0031).

schema_version.description: Envelope version. New optional payload fields do not change it; a breaking change does.

id.description: Event id, assigned by the emitter (the control plane or the node agent).

seq.description: Gap-free position in the event log, assigned by the primary when it accepts the event.

data.description: Type-specific payload. The schema for this object is fixed by `type` in the allOf below.

QuarantineId.description: Quarantined copy id (`qrn_` + ULID), generated by the node that keeps the copy.

RequestId.description: Correlation id of one API or MCP call (`req_` + ULID).

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, for example `2026-11-02T09:15:00Z`.

Scope.description: One scope, `<resource>:<verb>`; the complete list is in the contracts README.

Source.description: Where the event was emitted: the control plane itself, or a specific node.

Subject.description: The resource the event is about. `type` is the resource kind in the same words the id prefixes use (node, vm, app, deployment, build, domain, volume, backup, project, lease, grant, approval, incident, agent, user, cluster, webhook); `id` is that resource's id. For certificate and domain events the subject is the domain; for audit.chain_broken it is the cluster; for backup.* it is the backup; for restore.* it is the app; for volume.quarantined it is the volume.

Actor.description: Who caused the change, when the event was caused by an identifiable actor. Absent for events produced by observation only.

id.description: `usr_`, `agt_` or `nod_` id; `system` for the control plane itself.

Selector.description: Resource selector of a grant. A resource matches if it matches any listed entry; an app matches `projects` through its project. `{"all": true}` matches everything and `{}` matches nothing.

DeploymentPhase.description: Phase of a deployment. `build` is kept for compatibility and is never produced: a failed build is a `build.failed` event, because a deployment exists only once its build succeeded (ADR 0117).

BuildPhase.description: Phase a build was in when it failed or was cancelled (ADR 0117).

LeaseMode.description: Lease mode (D-0047). `local` for HA policy `none` and `cold`; `expiring` for `warm` and `hot`.

LeaseState.description: Lease state as seen by a node (node-agent protocol).

data_node_enrolled.description: A node completed enrollment. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_node_connected.description: A node's session started (D-0011). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

log_seq.description: Last change-log seq the node had verified when the session opened.

data_node_disconnected.description: A node's session ended or the node missed heartbeats. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_node_fenced.description: A node self-fenced its stateful apps after losing their leases (D-0019). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

fencing_tokens.description: The token of the fence for each lease in lease_ids, keyed by lease id: the highest token the node had seen for the lease when the fence started, which for a fence that a lease_revoke started is the revoke's token (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.5 step 2, ADR 0246). From M5b the node always sends it.

vm_ids.description: The VMs the fence stopped (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.5 step 3). From M5b the node always sends it.

data_node_fence_failed.description: A node could not confirm that a fence stopped every stateful VM bound to a lost lease, so a VM may still be running; the node marked itself failed and the lease stays unstartable until an operator acknowledges the fence with POST /api/v1/nodes/{node_id}/fence-ack (D-0074, D-0079). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

fencing_tokens.description: The token of the fence for each lease in lease_ids, keyed by lease id: the highest token the node had seen for the lease when the fence started, which for a fence that a lease_revoke started is the revoke's token (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.5 step 2, ADR 0246). From M5b the node always sends it.

error.description: The engine error of the forced stop.

data_node_disk_low.description: A node's free disk fell below its threshold (D-0032). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_vm_created.description: A VM was created. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_vm_started.description: A VM reached `running`. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_vm_stopped.description: A VM stopped on request. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_vm_crashed.description: A VM exited without being asked to stop. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_vm_deleted.description: A VM was deleted. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_created.description: An app was created. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_updated.description: An app's settings changed. `changed` lists the app field names that were written. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_deleted.description: An app was deleted. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_down.description: An app's health check failed past its threshold, or its VM crashed (D-0032). From M5a, for an app with more than one replica, the primary also emits it with `check: edge_health` when the edge has every instance out of rotation; `node_id` is then the edge's. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_degraded.description: An app with more than one replica has at least one instance out of the edge's rotation and at least one in it (ADR 0142, ADR 0143). Emitted by the control plane from the edge's status reports, when the app enters the degraded state and when the set of instances out of rotation changes. It opens no incident; `app.down` does once no instance is left. Recovery is `app.up` with `from: degraded`. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_up.description: An app recovered. `from` says whether it was `down` or, from M5a, `degraded`; an event without `from` comes from an older primary or node and means `down`. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_restarted.description: An app's instances were restarted. `restart_generation` is the new value of the app's counter. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_failed_over.description: The lease of a warm app moved to its warm node, which starts the app from its last complete copy (ADR 0175). Emitted by the control plane in the change that moves the lease; while the lease row carries the unsettled mark, the grant to the warm node follows once that change is replicated (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.4, ADR 0292); the actor is the caller of failoverApp. `snapshot_seq` is the copy the app starts from; writes made on the old node after it are not in it and are kept there as a quarantined copy when that node returns. Opens no incident. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

from_node_id.description: The node that held the lease.

to_node_id.description: The warm node, which holds the lease now.

fencing_token.description: Fencing token of the new lease.

snapshot_seq.description: The complete copy the app starts from.

snapshot_taken_at.description: When the old node took that snapshot, when the primary knows it.

grant_pending.description: True when the grant to the warm node waits for replication and majority support, so the app starts later (ADR 0292).

data_app_switched_over.description: A planned switchover of a warm app completed: the lease moved to its former warm node, which starts the app from a final snapshot taken while its writes were frozen, so no write was lost, and the former node is its warm copy (ADR 0177). Emitted by the control plane in the change that moves the lease; while the lease row carries the unsettled mark, the grant to the warm node follows once that change is replicated (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.4, ADR 0292); the actor is the caller of switchoverApp. Opens no incident. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

fencing_token.description: Fencing token of the new lease.

frozen_ms.description: Not sent; reserved. The event is emitted in the change that moves the lease, before the new instance runs, so the primary cannot measure how long the app's writes were frozen then.

grant_pending.description: True when the grant to the warm node waits for replication and majority support, so the app starts later (ADR 0292).

data_app_switchover_failed.description: A planned switchover of a warm app stopped before the lease moved (ADR 0177). `step` is where it stopped: `freeze` (the node could not pause the app or ship the final snapshot), `revoke` (the primary gave up before revoking the lease, for example because a node disconnected) or `move` (a step after the revoke failed: the source did not confirm that the app stopped, or the change that moves the lease could not be made). At `freeze` and `revoke` the primary sent the source `switchover_thaw`, unless a failed fence covers the lease or the lease is revoked in its own view (node-agent-protocol.md section 5.17), nothing moved, and the event opens no incident, except when the failed fence is the source's own: the app then stays down until `failoverApp` moves it, so the event opens an incident as at `move`, which that move's `app.failed_over` resolves. When a failed fence covers the lease, the app stays frozen, paused or stopped, until an operator acknowledges that fence, and after the source's own fence until `failoverApp` moves it. When the failed fence was another node's, the source still holds the lease, and the primary's next thaw resumes the app; when it was the source's own, the acknowledgement revokes the lease (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.5), no thaw resumes the app, and `failoverApp` moves it. At `move` the lease stays revoked, and the app stays stopped on its node or, when the node did not confirm the stop, may still be paused there, so the event opens an incident for the app unless such an incident of that app is open; `failoverApp` to the same warm node completes the move, once any failed fence is acknowledged, and its `app.failed_over` resolves that incident (node-agent-protocol.md section 6.13, permission-model.md section 8.2). Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_app_left_stopped.description: The app's HA policy left `warm` while the primary held a grant of its lease with a new token that it had not sent, such as a regrant from the holder's `hello` that waited for the lease's gate (a failover's waiting grant cannot be dropped: updateApp refuses to leave `warm` while `App.lease.grant_pending` is true). The primary dropped that grant, so the node it named may hold no lease for the app; when it holds none, the app stays stopped until an operator starts it, and `startApp` then grants that node the lease (node-agent-protocol.md section 8.4, "Ending the renewals" and "A holder that holds no lease"). Emitted by the control plane as it drops the grant, right after the change of the policy commits; the actor is the caller of updateApp. A primary that restarted after that change committed holds no such grant and emits none. Opens no incident. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

node_id.description: The node the dropped grant named.

fencing_token.description: The token of the dropped grant.

reason.description: Why the grant was dropped: the app's HA policy left `warm`.

data_app_vulnerable.description: The image an app runs has a new finding that is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog or has a CVSS base score of 9.0 or more (ADR 0138, ADR 0150). Emitted by the control plane when it records such a finding: after an image inventory arrives, or after a data refresh matches a new record. One event carries every qualifying finding of that match, at most 20 of them in `findings`, with `finding_count` the full number. It opens an incident for the app, separate from an `app.down` incident: an open `app.down` incident does not absorb it, and `app.up` does not resolve it. The system resolves it when the app has no open finding that qualifies (a deploy of a patched image, or corrected data), or a user or agent resolves it. Findings of Quoro's own components and of host kernels raise no event in M5a. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

reason.description: Why it qualifies: `kev` when it is in the KEV catalog, otherwise `cvss_critical`.

rebuildable.description: True when the app has a Git source, so a build with `refresh_base` can pick up a patched base; false for an image app, which needs a new upstream image.

data_deployment_started.description: A deployment began. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_deployment_succeeded.description: A deployment's instances are healthy. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_deployment_failed.description: A deployment failed at a named phase. A failed build is reported by `build.failed`, not here (ADR 0117). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_build_started.description: A build was created and queued for the app's node (ADR 0117). Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

ref.description: The branch, tag or commit the build was asked to build.

data_build_succeeded.description: A build produced its image on the node; the deployment it starts (`trigger: build`) follows with its own `deployment.started` (ADR 0117). Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_build_failed.description: A build failed: source checkout, a build step, export, import or its timeout (ADR 0117, ADR 0119). Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

failed_step.description: The BuildKit step that failed, when the build failed in a step.

data_build_cancelled.description: A build was cancelled before it finished. Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_backup_succeeded.description: A backup's seal was written: its snapshot is in the repository and can be restored (ADR 0147, ADR 0148). `app_id` and `volume_id` are absent for a control-plane backup. Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

pause_ms.description: How long the app was paused for a `pause_copy` snapshot; 0 for `reflink`.

data_backup_failed.description: A backup ended without a seal: snapshot, upload, a lost lease or a timeout (ADR 0147). It opens no incident; the next scheduled backup is still taken. Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_volume_quarantined.description: A node that lost a warm app's lease to a failover kept its divergent volume as a quarantined copy on its own disk (ADR 0176, node-agent-protocol.md section 9). Emitted by the control plane when it records the copy, with the system audit record `volume.quarantine`, and once per quarantine_id for a copy of a volume that is gone, which gets no row (ADR 0316). Opens no incident. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

node_id.description: The node that keeps the copy.

data_restore_succeeded.description: A volume backup was restored into a new volume on `node_id`, the node holds the app's new `local` lease and the app is started there (ADR 0147). Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

fencing_token.description: Fencing token of the new lease.

data_restore_failed.description: A restore did not complete: download, verification of a chunk, the seal or the manifest, or writing the volume (ADR 0147). The app stays stopped with no lease until the operator restores again or deletes the app. Emitted by the control plane. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_certificate_issued.description: A TLS certificate was obtained or renewed. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_certificate_expiring.description: A certificate expires within its warning window (D-0032). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_certificate_failed.description: Obtaining or renewing a certificate failed. A primary that does not yet emit `domain.unserved` (ADR 0167) also emits this event with `tls_mode` `tunnel` for a `tunnel` domain that no tunnel serves; `domain.unserved` replaces that use. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_domain_unserved.description: No machine can serve a domain's hostname although its app has an instance meant to run: the domain's `serving_status` became `unserved` (ADR 0167). `error` is the domain's `last_error`. Opens no incident. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_domain_served.description: A machine serves an `unserved` domain's hostname again: the domain's `serving_status` went from `unserved` to `serving` (ADR 0167). `unserved_since`, when the primary knows it, is when the domain became `unserved`, like `degraded_since` on `app.up`. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_grant_created.description: A grant was issued (D-0030). `kind` selects what authorized it: a standing grant, an incident, or an approval. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_grant_revoked.description: A grant was revoked; the agent loses its access within seconds (D-0030). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_grant_expired.description: A grant's TTL passed (`ttl`) or its uses ran out (`max_uses`). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_approval_requested.description: An agent filed an approval request for a destructive action (D-0030). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_approval_approved.description: A human approved a request; `grant_id` is the short-lived extra grant issued for it. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_approval_denied.description: A human denied a request. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_approval_expired.description: A request expired undecided. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_incident_opened.description: A detection opened an incident and scoped the grants that follow it (D-0032). Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

wake.description: Present only in a webhook delivery from a webhook with `wake` that issued an incident grant for this incident: the agent the delivery wakes and the incident grant it acts under (D-0032). Never in the event log (`GET /api/v1/events`, the event stream) and never in a test delivery. The delivery signature covers it like the rest of the body.

data_incident_resolved.description: An incident was resolved. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.

data_audit_chain_broken.description: Audit verification found a broken hash link (D-0031). `broken_at_seq` is the first record whose chain does not verify; `expected_hash` is the link the previous record implies and `found_hash` is the stored one. `reason` is one of the local verification reasons (`hash_mismatch`, `prev_mismatch`, `seq_gap`, audit-log-format.md section 6) or, from M5a, a disagreement with the off-site copy (audit-log-format.md section 8.3): `tail_truncated` when the local log ends before the last record the copy holds (`broken_at_seq` is the first missing `seq`, `expected_hash` its hash in the copy, `found_hash` 64 zeros), `copy_mismatch` when the local hash at an exported `seq` differs from the copy's (`expected_hash` is the copy's, `found_hash` the local one). An event without `reason` comes from a primary older than M5a. Payload fields are additive within schema_version 1.
